Interfaces / Development note

A good interface starts before JavaScript.

Content, links and structure first. Interactivity next. Progressive enhancement as a design and development decision.

By Sergio Hernández3 November 2026
In this note
  1. A foundation people can read
  2. Every control has a job
  3. Motion is a layer
  4. Test the foundation and its enhancements

A website can include animation, a 3D model and interactive controls while still being useful when those layers are unavailable. Progressive enhancement means building that foundation before adding effects.

A foundation people can read

The main content should exist in the document delivered to the browser. A heading, paragraph and link are useful on their own: they do not need to wait for a function to finish running.

On Alejandro’sTech, language routes, projects, experience and notes are generated as HTML. The browser enhances the experience with filters, animations and controls, but the information is already there.

Every control has a job

A link takes you somewhere; a button performs an action. Respecting that difference helps keyboard navigation, assistive technology and familiar browser behaviours work predictably.

Interaction also needs perceptible feedback: which technology is selected, whether an animation is paused or whether an address was copied. That state is part of the interface.

Motion is a layer

Animation can explain a relationship or give an identity character. It should also be possible to stop it. A reduced-motion preference, a hidden tab or an offscreen model are situations worth handling explicitly.

This website’s emblem retains a static alternative. The 3D layer adds depth and interaction; access to information remains grounded in HTML and real links.

Test the foundation and its enhancements

Review the page with and without its enhancements: reading on narrow screens, visible focus, keyboard navigation, link destinations and behaviour when a resource is unavailable.

A useful question is specific: can someone find what they need and take the next action? Visual effects should support that answer.

Putting it into practice

Start with a complete reading and navigation experience. Add interaction where it offers a function or a useful way to explore content.
